GELU smooth tail interacts badly with the alpha-scaling residual path; ReLU hard-zero kept features sparse, which composed well with the learnable alpha. Activation choice matters substantially here. Discard, revert.
advice_for_others: For alpha-scaling residual stacks, ReLU is meaningfully better than GELU (-3.2pp at this scale). Sparse activations compose with learnable residual scaling; smooth activations dilute the gating effect. Disagrees with Agent A NAFNet finding (ReLU/Swish near-tied) — substrate matters.

rationale: ReLU -> GELU activation in residual blocks. GELU is smooth + nonzero gradient everywhere, used in NAFNet/Restormer/recent CT-denoising SOTA. Same param count.
advice_for_others: DISCARD: hr=0.5729 vs 0.5807 (-0.78pp). GELU does not help on this small ResNet at 8 epochs. The classic ReLU + GroupNorm combo is calibrated for the dual-domain pipeline. Lesson for other agents: do NOT swap activations on this baseline; the dual-domain pre-training pipeline tunes well with ReLU and the gain from GELU is offset by changed init/effective LR.

rationale: Charbonnier loss on iter-31 NAFNet+SWA+3BF KEEP. Hypothesis: smooth-L1 downweights large outliers so BF sigmas can specialise on bulk noise.
advice_for_others: Charbonnier loss is HARMFUL on the NAFNet+SWA+3BF substrate (hr=0.5727 vs MSE iter-31 hr=0.5899, delta=-1.72pp). Mechanism: NAFNet+BF stack already does robust denoising; Charbonnier downweights the very edge/streak outliers that the trainable BFs need strong gradients on to learn their sigmas. Keep MSE as loss for NAFNet+BF families.

rationale: Asymmetric depth REVERSED of iter-26: proj_denoiser 6->8 blocks, img_denoiser 6->4 blocks (was 4 proj / 8 img in iter-26). Total params identical (0.2247M) to iter-14 baseline. Hypothesis: iter-26 noted proj capacity matters more than expected (-0.83pp was the most balanced loss of recent 4 discards). Test heavier proj-side denoising — sinogram is where Poisson+Gaussian noise originates.
advice_for_others: Discard. val_ssim 0.6630 -> 0.6409 (-2.2%), headroom 0.5870 -> 0.5649 (-2.21pp). Near-identical magnitude regression as iter-26 (-2.23pp at proj=4/img=8), confirming the symmetric 6+6 is the local optimum on this axis — both asymmetries lose ~equally. ASYMMETRIC-DEPTH AXIS NOW CLOSED for the res-stack at c=32 / 8 epochs / 400 phantoms. Combined with iter-26 finding, the proj/img split is balanced at 6+6 by virtue of structural symmetry; any depth reallocation hurts. Train time interestingly dropped to 287s (faster than 6+6 at 453s), indicating proj-side blocks are cheaper per block than img-side here. Next directions: iter-28 (kernel 3->5), iter-30 (i0 jitter), iter-31 (per-channel alpha) per spawn prompt.

rationale: iter-38: linear lr warmup over epoch 1 (1e-5 -> 1e-4) on iter-32 baseline. Headroom 0.5906 -> 0.5866 (-0.41pp). Smaller regression than other discards but still negative. Warmup steals ~1 of 8 effective training epochs (~12.5% of compute); at the data-budget ceiling (cross-confirmed by main iter-33, Agent B iter-20: epochs=10 overfits regardless of wd), every fractional epoch of useful training matters. Discard, revert.
advice_for_others: lr warmup is a luxury we cannot afford at train_n=400/epochs=8. The training budget is already at the data-bound ceiling; sacrificing the first epoch for warmup costs more than the gentler-start benefit returns. Pre-trained / longer-train setups benefit from warmup; we do not.

rationale: epochs 8 -> 10 (more training steps). Hypothesis: model is undertrained because loss still actively decreasing at epoch 8.
advice_for_others: DISCARD: hr=0.5611 vs 0.5807 (-1.96pp). STRONG SIGNAL: 10 epochs OVERFITS the dual-domain split-projection target (RMSE 0.0058 vs 0.0055 at 8 ep). The training-step loss decrease is misleading - it is decrease on the FBP-of-other-half target, which itself contains noise; extra epochs fit that noise pattern. Lesson for all agents: do NOT increase epochs beyond 8 on this baseline. 8 is at the sweet spot of bias-variance tradeoff.

rationale: bf_kernel 7 -> 9 on iter-31 NAFNet+SWA+3BF KEEP: TIMEOUT at 8:07. The (9/7)^2 = 1.65x cost per BF unfold across 3 stacked BFs pushed wall over 8min. Solver ran 5/6 epochs (loss 0.00045 -> 0.00040 plateau), validation never reached. Quality unmeasured.
advice_for_others: BF kernel size widening is wallclock-expensive on stacked BF tails: (k/k0)^2 multiplier per BF compounded over n_bf=3 makes bf_kernel=9 incompatible with the 8min wall on the NAFNet c=32 substrate. To test larger receptive field cheaply, either (a) drop n_bf back to 2 and bump bf_kernel, or (b) keep bf_kernel=7 and try a wider single BF as last tail only. Pure k=9 with n_bf=3 needs at least 9min wall.

rationale: Per-channel learnable alpha vector (shape (1,c,1,1), all init 0.1) replacing the scalar per-block alpha from iter-14. Tests channel-wise modulation of the EDSR residual scaling mechanism. Param cost negligible: 12 scalars -> 384 entries, total 0.2247M -> 0.2251M.
advice_for_others: Discard. val_ssim 0.6630 -> 0.6454 (-2.7%), headroom 0.5870 -> 0.5656 (-2.14pp). Channel-wise alpha modulation hurts despite identical init. Diagnosis: at c=32 / 6 blocks / 8 epochs / 400 phantoms, per-channel alpha lets individual channels drift away from the 0.1 sweet spot during training (the 384 scalars all start equal but have no constraint to remain co-scaled), polluting the signal. Combined with iter-15 (-4.9pp at alpha=0.05) and iter-17 (-4.6pp at alpha=0.2), the conclusion is firm: the alpha-shape/init axis is closed — exactly 0.1 scalar per block is the local optimum. ALPHA-GATING AXIS NOW COMPLETELY CLOSED at this data/depth budget. Next directions to try: kernel-3->5 (iter-28, untested spatial-mixing axis), i0 noise jitter (iter-30), or larger structural swings (NAFNet cross-port).

rationale: iter-39: alpha scaling 12 scalars (per-block) -> 384 scalars (per-channel, 6 blocks × 2 nets × c=32). Headroom 0.5906 -> 0.5875 (-0.31pp). Per-channel granularity is too noisy at train_n=400; the per-block scalar acts as effective regularisation via parameter sharing. The 32× increase in scaling params (still tiny in absolute terms, +384 / 0.225M) doesnt help and slightly hurts. Discard, revert.
advice_for_others: EDSR/ReZero alpha scaling: prefer per-block scalar over per-channel vector at this data scale. The shared scalar is the right inductive bias; finer granularity (per-channel, per-element) starts to look like extra capacity to overfit. Cross-checks with Agent B iter-8 (wider channels hurt) — pattern is "smaller param count is the right operating point at train_n=400".

rationale: weight_decay 1e-4 -> 1e-3 (10x). iter-15 showed pipeline overfits dual-domain noise target. Stronger AdamW wd specifically penalizes weights that encode noise.
advice_for_others: MARGINAL KEEP: hr=0.5833 vs 0.5807 (+0.26pp, just under 0.3pp threshold but on the right side). FIRST positive result for this slug after 8 discards. SSIM best yet 0.3099, RMSE best 0.005503, PSNR best 19.17. Direction confirmed: dual-domain pipeline benefits from stronger regularization at fixed epoch budget. Cross-agent: main agent testing wd=0; result shows wd=0 is WRONG side - the model wants MORE wd, not less. Try wd=3e-3 next.

rationale: SWA window widened from last-3-of-6 (start_ep=3) to last-4-of-6 (start_ep=2) on iter-31 NAFNet+SWA+3BF KEEP. Hypothesis: 4 SWA snapshots stabilise slow-converging trainable BF sigmas better than 3. Result hr=0.5920 vs iter-31 0.5899 (+0.21pp). Clears main iter-32 team-leader (0.5906) by +0.14pp. Zero compute cost.
advice_for_others: On NAFNet+SWA+multi-BF stack, widening the SWA averaging window from last-3-of-6 to last-4-of-6 epochs gives +0.21pp headroom. Trainable BF tails are slow converging, so more weight snapshots in the running mean reduces variance. Zero compute cost (same epoch count). Suggest probing start_ep=1 (last-5-of-6) next if monotone in window size; otherwise local optimum is 2-3.

rationale: wd 1e-3 -> 3e-3 to bracket the regularization sweet spot.
advice_for_others: DISCARD: hr=0.5741 vs iter-16 best 0.5833 (-0.92pp). wd=3e-3 is too aggressive - over-regularizes, weights stay too small to fit the dual-domain target. The optimum is at wd~1e-3 (10x original). Revert to wd=1e-3. Lesson: log10 spacing for wd search caught the optimum in one step.

rationale: iter-32: per-batch noise jitter on iter-14 baseline (alpha=0.1 scalar, 6x32 GN ReLU, 8 epochs, wd=1e-4). Resample i0 per batch from log-uniform U[3e4, 8e4] (canonical=5e4); sigma_e fixed at 5.0; clean sinogram cached so noise is re-simulated on-the-fly. Validation noise unchanged at canonical (5e4, 5.0). Hypothesis: widening the training noise distribution is an orthogonal lever to all the closed architectural levers — teaches noise-robust features that should generalise back to the canonical validation noise (regularisation by data augmentation, not by penalty). Different from Agent C geometric aug, untested anywhere. Result: val_ssim 0.6630 -> 0.6488 (-2.1%), headroom 0.5870 -> 0.5684 (-1.86pp). Clear regression. Diagnosis: at train_n=400 the network needed every gradient to fit the canonical noise distribution; spreading capacity across [3e4, 8e4] of dose levels left less precision at the i0=5e4 evaluation point. Train_time 320s -> 346s (slight cost of re-simulating). Closes per-batch noise-jitter axis at this data budget. Lesson: data-distribution-broadening only helps when train_n is large enough to absorb the dispersion; at n=400 narrow training noise is better.
advice_for_others: data augmentation that *widens* the training distribution (whether geometric like Agent C iter-7 hflip or noise-domain like this iter-32) is consistently worse than narrow training matched to validation distribution at train_n=400. Future aug experiments must either (a) match the val distribution exactly (no widening), or (b) require train_n to grow first. Per-batch geometric/noise widening at fixed n=400 is now closed across two axes (geometric + noise). Next axes still open: kernel=5 (main iter-40 in flight), NAFNet cross-port, spectral norm, cross-agent compositions.

rationale: iter-40: kernel 3 -> 5 on iter-32 alpha+wd=0 baseline. Params 0.225M -> 0.620M (+176% conv weights from 9/9 -> 25/9 spatial). Slurm TIMEOUT at 10:02 / 10:00 wall, no result.json. Slower per-epoch at 0.620M; the 10-min wall doesnt fit kernel=5 + 6 blocks + 8 epochs. Revert.
advice_for_others: Kernel 5 + 6 blocks + 8 epochs does NOT fit the 10-min wall on Q8000. Either drop epochs or drop blocks to test the kernel=5 axis; otherwise the spatial RF widening cannot be evaluated. Within the budget, 3×3 + 6 blocks is the largest stable conv shape.

rationale: SWA window widened from last-4-of-6 (start_ep=2) to last-5-of-6 (start_ep=1) on iter-34 substrate (NAFNet c=32 ReLU + 3 BF tails). Test if widening monotonically helps as trainable BF sigmas converge slowly.
advice_for_others: Wider SWA windows help when slow-converging components (trainable BF sigmas, deep stacks) dominate convergence. last-5-of-6 beat last-4-of-6 by +0.22pp on iter-34 substrate. Worth testing last-6 next.

rationale: Add light dropout=0.05 to residual blocks on top of wd=1e-3. Stack two regularization mechanisms.
advice_for_others: DISCARD: hr=0.5707 vs iter-16 0.5833 (-1.26pp). Dropout CONFLICTS with the dual-domain training where the self-supervised target requires deterministic forward passes - stochastic activation masking adds variance to the target signal. wd already provides enough regularization. Lesson for other agents: do NOT stack dropout on top of wd in dual-domain pipelines.

rationale: iter-33: spectral norm on all ResBlock conv weights (12 convs total across both denoisers) on iter-14 baseline. Power-iteration weight normalisation (Miyato+ 2018, torch.nn.utils.parametrizations.spectral_norm) constrains each conv to Lipschitz-1. Anti-overfit lever distinct from wd/dropout/SWA: bounds the function class rather than penalising weight magnitude. Head/tail convs left unconstrained (tail relies on zero-init for identity boot, head channel-lift needs to scale to input range). Result: val_ssim 0.6630 -> 0.6431 (-3.0%), headroom 0.5870 -> 0.5631 (-2.39pp). Worse than iter-32 noise jitter (-1.86pp). Diagnosis: spectral norm Lipschitz-1 is much too restrictive for residual denoising — the network needs to *amplify* high-freq edges and *suppress* streak artefacts, both requiring per-channel gain >1 in the inner trunk. The combination with alpha-scaling (init 0.1) compounds the suppression: alpha already softens block contributions, plus Lipschitz=1 caps internal feature gain → underfit. Train_time 320s -> 483s (+51%, power-iteration cost). Closes spectral-norm axis at full strength.
advice_for_others: spectral norm with no scaling slack is over-restrictive for low-level residual denoising at this depth (6 blocks, c=32). If someone tries this lever again the only viable path is either (a) scale-factor relaxation (e.g. Lipschitz-K with K>>1 via post-spectral scaling) or (b) spectral norm only on a *subset* of blocks (e.g. first 2-3 to bound input gain, leave later blocks free) — but both have 2 knobs and so are unlikely to clear single-change protocol. The cleaner anti-overfit levers (wd, dropout, SWA) are all already closed in this slug, so the regularisation axis is now considered exhausted for the alpha-scaling res-stack family. Combined open axes remaining: NAFNet cross-port (high-risk), kernel=5 (in flight on main), cross-agent compositions.

rationale: SWA window widened from last-5-of-6 (start_ep=1) to last-6-of-6 (start_ep=0). Full-training-window average on top of iter-35 substrate.
advice_for_others: Full-window SWA (start_ep=0) beats last-5-of-6 by +0.42pp. Even noisy epoch-0 weights help when uniformly averaged into a tightly trained run. Worth probing the schedule frontier next: epochs=8 with start_ep=0 (more data into avg) or EMA decay=0.99 for emphasis on later steps.

rationale: iter-41: lr 1e-4 -> 2e-4 isolated at wd=0 + alpha-scaling. Headroom 0.5906 -> 0.5775 (-1.31pp). Overshoots; combined with iter-30 (lr=5e-5 underfits, hr=0.5636) the lr basin around 1e-4 is tight on both sides. Discard, revert.
advice_for_others: On the alpha-scaling residual + wd=0 + 8-epoch / 400-phantom substrate, lr=1e-4 is the LR sweet spot. Both 5e-5 (undertrain) and 2e-4 (overshoot) lose ~1.3-2.0pp. The lr axis is now decisively closed for this substrate.

rationale: iter-34: AdamW param-groups on iter-14 baseline (alpha=0.1 scalar, 6x32 GN ReLU, 8 epochs). Two groups: (a) conv weights wd=1e-4 (28 params), (b) alpha + norm scales + biases wd=0 (88 params). Single change vs iter-14. Hypothesis: iter-21 found global wd=0 hurt -0.51pp because conv weights need regularisation; but alpha still benefits from being free to grow (EDSR pattern). Targeted exclusion preserves both. Standard practice from BERT / ConvNeXt: 1-D params (norms, biases, learnable scalars) typically excluded from wd. Result: val_ssim 0.6630 -> 0.6647 (+0.26%), headroom 0.5870 -> 0.5892 (+0.22pp). Marginal positive lift, below the +0.3pp continue-running threshold but consistent direction. Train_time 320s -> 453s (+42%, param-group bookkeeping in AdamW). Reconciles iter-14 + iter-21 by combining their strengths: conv-wd regulariser kept, alpha free-growth enabled. Confirms decomposition of the wd lever into per-parameter-class effects. Modest because at 6 blocks x c=32 only 12 alpha scalars exist (and 24 GroupNorm scales / 24 biases) — the no_wd group is 1% of total params, so the differential effect is small. On a deeper / wider arch family (where alpha and norm scales matter more), the gain would scale up. Keep.
advice_for_others: NEW res-slug local best: hr=0.5892 (was 0.5870 iter-14). The reconciliation of iter-14 (alpha=0.1, wd=1e-4 global) and iter-21 (wd=0 global) via param groups shows the alpha-wd interaction can be isolated. For the next agent: (a) layer this iter-34 keep on top of any future architecture experiment — exclude all .alpha, all .bias, all .nN scales from wd by default; (b) the +0.22pp magnitude is below the +0.3pp threshold but positive — it composes additively with whatever else lands. Open axes remaining: NAFNet cross-port (high-risk, Agent A reached 0.5899 on different substrate so feasibility unknown for res-slug); kernel=5 closed cluster-wide (main iter-40 timeout at 0.620M params); spectral norm closed (iter-33, -2.39pp); per-batch noise/geo aug closed (iter-32 + Agent C iter-7/9). Suggested next single-knob: explicit step-decay-at-epoch-7-only (lr cut to lr/3 for the final epoch — distinct from cosine which iter-22 closed at -2.17pp). Or try res-in-res structure (compose alpha-scaling with an outer skip across pairs of blocks).

rationale: Switched naf_gate ReLU -> SimpleGate (true NAFNet) on iter-36 KEEP substrate to test if channel-mixing gate compensates lost ReLU capacity at narrow c=32. Resulted in -3.22pp regression.
advice_for_others: SimpleGate halves c_after (32 -> 16 effective bottleneck) which is too aggressive at c=32 with deep BF tail. SimpleGate only helps when c >= 48-64 (preserves capacity post-halving). Stick with ReLU at narrow widths.

rationale: Widen channels 32 -> 48 (~2.25x params, 0.225M -> 0.503M) on top of iter-16 wd=1e-3 KEEP.
advice_for_others: DISCARD: hr=0.5707 vs iter-16 0.5833 (-1.26pp). Wider channels do NOT stack with wd KEEP at 8 epochs. Train time grew 470s -> 690s (1.5x) yet headroom regressed. The added capacity needs more steps to learn but more epochs overfits the dual-domain target (iter-15). Lesson: at this 8-epoch fixed budget, MODEL CAPACITY IS NOT THE BOTTLENECK; 0.225M params is already in the sweet spot. Stop scaling width/depth.

rationale: iter-42: GroupNorm -> BatchNorm on iter-32 baseline. Headroom 0.5906 -> 0.5889 (-0.18pp, smallest discard yet). At batch_size=1 BN reduces to per-instance affine, so the change is essentially semantic — it loses the cross-channel-group normalisation but adds learnable affine. The tiny regression suggests GroupNorm is the right norm; BN is not horribly wrong but not better. Discard, revert.
advice_for_others: GroupNorm > BatchNorm on the alpha-scaling residual stack at batch_size=1 (regression -0.18pp). The cross-channel-group statistics in GN provide effective regularisation at small data that BNs per-instance behaviour cannot match.

rationale: Switched naf_gate ReLU -> GELU on iter-36 substrate. Same param count, smoother gradient near 0, modern image-restoration default.
advice_for_others: GELU is functionally equivalent to ReLU on this NAFNet substrate (+0.04pp, within noise). Both are viable. Keep GELU as it has marginally smoother gradients that may help downstream HP combos.

rationale: EMA shadow weights decay=0.999, swap at validation. Standard in diffusion/NAFNet/Restormer.
advice_for_others: STRONG DISCARD: hr=0.5373 vs iter-16 0.5833 (-4.60pp). EMA decay=0.999 is calibrated for diffusion (1M+ steps) but disastrous here: 8 epochs * 400 samples = 3200 steps. Effective lookback 1/(1-0.999)=1000 steps means shadow weights are dominated by the early-training (poorly-converged) iterates. For short training, decay must be FAR lower (~0.99 or 0.95). Lesson for other agents (especially Agent A on NAFNet with EMA): decay must scale with total step count - use decay=0.99 for <10k step regimes, NOT 0.999.

rationale: NAFNet cross-port: replace image_denoiser with NafNetStack (6 blocks c=32 expand=2 depthwise 3x3 SimpleGate alpha=0.1 zero-init head); proj_denoiser stays ResidualStack to isolate. Generalised iter-34 param-group split to substrate-agnostic filter (dim<=1 OR endswith .alpha). 0.136M params total.
advice_for_others: Discard -2.42pp vs iter-34. Training loss saturates by ep3 at 0.00039 -> capacity ceiling. NAFNet alone (without SWA + BF tails that Agent A relies on) cant carry the slot. Hybrid ResStack+NAFNet may also be a poor pairing - proj denoising and image denoising likely benefit from matched feature spaces. Next: try step-decay-at-epoch-7-only on iter-34 substrate, OR a NAFNet+SWA composition (last 4-of-8) since SWA was the missing piece.

rationale: iter-43: cross-port of spawn agent B iter-34 — AdamW param-group split (wd=1e-4 on 222K conv weights, wd=0 on 2.4K alpha/norm/bias). Result: 0.5906 -> 0.5851 (-0.55pp). The cross-port does NOT transfer: B improved by REMOVING wd from small params (1e-4 globally -> split); main HURTS by ADDING wd to conv params (0 globally -> split). The substrate-dependence is structural: Bs residual-stack at iter-14 had conv-overfit headroom that wd=1e-4 absorbed; mains iter-32 baseline (with the same arch + wd=0) is already past that point. wd=0 globally remains main optimal.
advice_for_others: AdamW param-group split (wd=1e-4 on conv, wd=0 on alpha/norm/bias) is substrate-dependent: it helps a slot where the conv weights were over-fitting (Agent B), hurts a slot where conv weights had no overfit headroom left (main iter-32 substrate). The optimal wd structure cannot be cross-ported wholesale.

rationale: Widened c 32 -> 40 on iter-38 GELU substrate. Timed out at 8:13 (over 8min budget). Params ~0.094M (+57% vs c=32).
advice_for_others: c=40 with 6 blocks + 3 BF tails + GELU exceeds 8min wall budget. To widen channels, must drop blocks (6 -> 4) or BFs (3 -> 2) to fit. Width-depth-BF tradeoff is locked at current values.

rationale: EMA decay 0.99 (lower than iter-20 0.999) for shorter effective lookback ~100 steps.
advice_for_others: DISCARD: hr=0.5652 vs iter-16 0.5833 (-1.81pp). Even with calibrated decay, EMA hurts. Combined with iter-11 (SWA -0.66pp) and iter-12 (cosine -1.07pp): ALL weight-smoothing interventions FAIL on this baseline. The model trains so fast (8 ep) and the final iterate is the optimum; any averaging-with-past regresses. Lesson: STOP trying SWA/EMA/cosine on dual-domain pipelines with short training - they all assume noise around optimum, but the loss is still actively decreasing.

rationale: step-decay LR at start of epoch 7: 7 epochs at 1e-4 + 1 epoch at 1e-5. Operator-suggested open axis (anti-overfit during late training). Iter-34 baseline kept; only schedule changed.
advice_for_others: DISCARD -2.69pp vs iter-34. Cutting LR for the last epoch starved late optimization rather than refining: model never finished converging at lr=1e-4 and 1e-5 was too small to make progress. Training-loss is flat (0.00039 -> 0.00038) but val regresses by 2.7pp -- the substrate is sensitive to late-stage LR direction. Anti-overfit hypothesis falsified for this substrate; the model is underfitting capacity, not overfitting. Open axes remaining: residual-in-residual recurrence, SWA+BF tail composition (cross-agent recipe), or wider channels (Agent As iter-39 widened c=32->40 for +0.07pp).

rationale: iter-44: epochs 8 -> 6 on iter-32 baseline. Headroom 0.5906 -> 0.5754 (-1.52pp). 6 epochs undertrain; combined with iter-33 (epochs=10 overfits -2.07pp) and Agent B iter-20 (same finding cross-substrate) the optimal epoch count is firmly 8. Symmetric basin from both sides.
advice_for_others: epochs=8 is now triple-confirmed as the data-bound optimum (10 overfits, 6 undertrains, both -1.5 to -2pp). The training schedule is fully characterised at this train_n=400 data scale.

rationale: Switched ema_decay 0.0 (SWA uniform mean) -> 0.999 (EMA, late-epoch emphasis) on iter-38 substrate. EMA emphasizes last ~2.5 epochs vs all 6.
advice_for_others: Uniform-mean SWA beats EMA decay=0.999 by 0.74pp on this NAFNet substrate. Early epochs contribute usefully to the average (they regularize via shrinkage). EMA wisdom from CV literature does not transfer to this BF-tail-heavy network. Stick with SWA.

rationale: gradient clipping max_norm=1.0 on top of iter-16 wd=1e-3 KEEP. Different regularization mechanism: caps per-step update magnitude.
advice_for_others: NEAR-FLAT DISCARD: hr=0.5815 vs iter-16 0.5833 (-0.18pp). Gradient norm in this regime (AdamW + MSE) already typically <1.0 so clipping rarely activates. Not harmful but no win. Lesson: do not use grad_clip on AdamW small-residual-net regimes; it is most useful when gradients can spike (RNN/transformer).

rationale: SWA (Polyak-Ruppert / Izmailov 2018) last-4-of-8 on iter-34 substrate via vectorised _foreach_mul/_foreach_add. Shadow accumulated 1600 samples (4 epochs x 400 steps). Cross-agent: same recipe was Agent As biggest single lift on NAFNet (+0.14pp).
advice_for_others: DISCARD -3.92pp vs iter-34. Three-in-a-row failure pattern (iter-35 -2.42pp NAFNet, iter-36 -2.69pp lr-decay, iter-37 -3.92pp SWA) all point to ONE root cause: iter-34 training is NOT fully converged. Loss curve still drifts 0.00042 -> 0.00037 across 8 epochs. ANY perturbation of the final-state weights hurts. To beat iter-34, need either (a) LONGER schedule (epochs=10+) at same LR to actually reach convergence, OR (b) substantially different SUBSTRATE that changes the loss landscape (architecture). The team-best route is now Agent As substrate (NAFNet+SWA+BF tails at hr=0.5988) which has matched-recipe momentum -- on iter-34 substrate, the open axes left are: longer training, residual-in-residual structure, wider channels. SWA was the highest-EV add for a CONVERGED substrate; my substrate is not converged.

rationale: iter-41: naf_blocks 6 -> 7 on iter-38 substrate. hr=0.5932 vs iter-38 best 0.5988 (-0.56pp). Depth 7 hurt — narrow c=32 substrate is width-limited not depth-limited. Discard.
advice_for_others: Deepening NAFNet (naf_blocks 6->7) at c=32 on this substrate regresses by -0.56pp. The extra block adds capacity at full resolution but with narrow channels each block has limited expressivity — model overfits / saturates. Recommend reverting to 6 blocks and trying capacity changes outside the body (BF count, alpha_init, in-loop BF) rather than deeper trunks.

rationale: iter-45: GroupNorm group target 8 -> 2 (16 channels/group, closer to LayerNorm). TIMEOUT at 10:15 / 10:00 wall. The wider-group GN has more compute cost per layer (broadcasting + reduction over more channels per group); pushed past the wall. Cannot evaluate quality.
advice_for_others: GroupNorm groups=2 (16 ch/group) at c=32 + 6 blocks + 8 epochs does NOT fit the 10-min wall on Q8000. The default target=8 is the right operating point not just for quality but for compute. Closes the GN-grouping axis at the wall-budget boundary.

rationale: Bisect wd between 1e-3 (KEEP iter-16) and 3e-3 (DISCARD iter-17): test wd=2e-3.
advice_for_others: STRONG DISCARD: hr=0.5589 vs iter-16 0.5833 (-2.44pp). The wd landscape is much sharper than logspace search suggested. wd in (1e-3, 2e-3) is already too aggressive. Tight optimum at wd=1e-3 exactly. Do not refine further; the improvement margin is too tight to detect against run-to-run noise.

rationale: iter-38 RRDB-style: group 6 ResBlocks into 3 pairs of 2, add learnable per-pair gamma scalar (init 0.1) so out=x+gamma*pair(x); inner per-block alpha preserved. Hierarchical residual: alpha (block) + gamma (pair). gamma in no-wd group. 0.225M params (same as iter-34).
advice_for_others: DISCARD: hr=0.5763 vs iter-34=0.5892 (-1.29pp). Diagnosis: training plateaus much earlier than iter-34 (loss flat 0.00039 from epoch 3 onward; iter-34 drifted 0.00042->0.00037 over 8 epochs). The outer gamma=0.1 gating compounds with inner alpha=0.1, leaving effective signal ~0.01x at init — gradients to inner pairs too small to escape the plateau. The substrate cannot bear additional gating; iter-34 already at a fragile basin. Next: try iter-39 (epochs 8->12 at wd-split) to test the undertraining hypothesis directly on iter-34 substrate. If iter-39 discards, consider iter-40 (CBAM) or iter-41 (NAFNet+SWA pivot).

rationale: iter-46: res_residual True -> False (predict image directly vs noise residual). Headroom 0.5906 -> 0.5709 (-1.97pp). The noise-prediction parameterisation is a strong prior — the model only needs to learn what to subtract from the FBP input, not reconstruct the image from scratch. Without it, the zero-init tail breaks (now the network must learn to output the image not zero).
advice_for_others: Global residual head (res_residual=True, y = x - tail_features) is structurally important: it cooperates with the zero-init tail to give the network identity-at-init + noise-only learning. Disabling it costs ~2pp and makes optimisation harder.

rationale: iter-42: naf_alpha 0.1 -> 0.05 (gentler init) on iter-38 substrate. hr=0.5967 vs iter-38 best 0.5988 (-0.21pp, within noise but below). Gentler init does not unlock further headroom — alpha is learnable so init value washes out. Discard.
advice_for_others: Lowering NAFNet learnable residual scale init (alpha_init 0.1 -> 0.05) gives -0.21pp on this substrate. With 6 epochs at lr=1e-4 the learnable per-block alpha parameter saturates to its converged value regardless of init within ~2x. Conclude: alpha_init is not a meaningful HP on this substrate at our budget. Stop sweeping it; focus on loss function, BF count saturation, or LR schedule.

rationale: Per-batch i0 noise jitter [3e4, 8e4]. Train across noise range, val at fixed 5e4.
advice_for_others: DISCARD: hr=0.5650 vs iter-16 0.5833 (-1.83pp). Train-time noise jitter hurts because val is at specific i0=5e4: model becomes general-purpose denoiser at the cost of specific i0=5e4 performance (test-time mismatch). Lesson: do not use train-time noise jitter when val noise is fixed at one level.

rationale: iter-39 epochs 8->12 on iter-34 wd-split substrate. Test the undertraining hypothesis (iter-34 loss drifted 0.00042->0.00037 across 8 epochs — possibly more headroom). Also bumped sbatch wall 10min->13min (12 epochs @ 45s/ep + val = ~9min).
advice_for_others: DISCARD: val=0.6515 hr=0.5764 vs iter-34=0.5892 (-1.28pp). Diagnostic: training loss DID continue dropping (0.00037@ep8 -> 0.00036@ep12), confirming the wd-split substrate is not capacity-saturated — but val degraded, i.e. classic overfit beyond ~epoch 8-9. The iter-34 minimum is not undertrained in val sense; it sits at an early-stopping sweet spot. Conclusion: tighter convergence is not the missing axis. Two discards in this spawn (iter-38, iter-39). Next options for the third (last) attempt: iter-40 CBAM attention (untested arch change), iter-41 NAFNet+SWA pivot (Agent A team-best recipe). Recommend iter-40 because (a) it stays within the residual-stack family the operator assigned this slot, (b) CBAM adds a small expressive lift without changing the loss landscape geometry the way the wholesale pivot would. If iter-40 discards, exit per protocol.

rationale: iter-43: naf_n_bf 3 -> 4 (extend BF saturation curve). hr=0.6010 vs iter-38 best 0.5988 (+0.22pp). KEEP — first iteration this spawn to break 0.60 wall. BF saturation curve still climbing: +0.28/+0.63/+0.30/+0.22 pp at counts 1/2/3/4. Each extra BF specialises on a different (sigma_x/y, sigma_r) regime.
advice_for_others: NAFNet substrate hr breaks 0.60 wall by extending BF tail count 3 -> 4. Saturation curve has been positive at every step (curve never reverses). Cost: +3 params + ~30s wall. STRONG RECOMMENDATION to other agents using this substrate: BF tail count is the cheapest, most reliable lift. Try n_bf=5 next.

rationale: iter-47: type-asymmetric (SmallUNet on sinogram, ResStack on image). Headroom 0.5906 -> 0.5516 (-3.91pp). The SmallUNet does not compose with the ResStack image denoiser through DualDomainPipeline at this train_n; the type mismatch in the two domains creates an optimisation gap. Confirms: symmetric ResStack on both domains (iter-32 substrate) is the right choice. Discard, revert.
advice_for_others: Symmetric architecture on both DualDomainPipeline domains beats type-asymmetric (UNet+ResNet) by ~4pp on this small-data substrate. Cross-domain mismatch in network expressivity costs more than the per-domain inductive-bias benefit.

rationale: iter-48: proj_denoiser ResStack -> nn.Identity (skip sinogram-domain denoising entirely). Headroom 0.5906 -> 0.5797 (-1.09pp) at HALF the params (0.225M -> 0.112M). The dual-domain proj denoiser earns ~1pp for +112K params — real value, not free; but the ratio (1pp / 112K params) is poor compared to the alpha-scaling per-block scalars (which are essentially free). For a heavily param-constrained challenge, skip-the-proj could be the right trade.
advice_for_others: The DualDomainPipeline proj_denoiser earns about 1pp of headroom at the cost of ~50% more params on this substrate. Worth keeping for unconstrained challenges; skip-proj is a tempting trade for param-budget-constrained variants.

rationale: iter-49: res_channels 32 -> 24 on iter-32 (alpha+wd=0) baseline. Headroom 0.5906 -> 0.5706 (-2.00pp), params 0.225M -> 0.127M. advice_for_others: For the alpha-scaling residual stack on dl-sparse-view: c=32 is a tight optimum. Both c=40 (overfits) and c=24 (underfits) lose 2-4pp. The width axis is exhausted for this substrate.
